name: Hole-in-the-Wall
blurb: A sea-carved arch at the north end of Rialto Beach; at low tide you can walk right through it to tide pools crowded with sea stars and anemones.

name: Rialto Beach
blurb: Storms heave whole tree trunks onto this cobbled shore across the Quillayute River from La Push; Hole-in-the-Wall waits 1.5 miles north.

name: Second Beach (Olympic coast)
blurb: A 0.7-mile forest trail and steep stairs drop to this sandy crescent studded with sea stacks, walled in by headlands you can't round even at the lowest tide.

name: Alki Beach
blurb: The Denny Party came ashore here on a stormy November day in 1851; now it's Seattle's summer sand strip, with views from the downtown skyline to the Olympics.
